provenance.inputs_seen_by_extractor: this evaluation's body text only (no paper, no model output)

issues.text: The report notes that the paper does not write the government's Lagrangian, and that the shadow price of the budget constraint (lambda) and its role in the MVPF should be discussed more fully, since the MVPF is essentially a cost-benefit ratio whose shadow prices of costs and benefits are not addressed.
issues.quote: This should be discussed better in the paper. The paper does not write the government Lagrangian, that would be helpful for the reader and to discuss the role of $\lambda$.

issues.text: The report argues that the paper's claim that a Pigouvian tax has an MVPF equal to one holds only if lump-sum taxation is possible (lambda equals u'); with deadweight losses in other taxes (lambda greater than u'), the Pigouvian tax would have MVPF below one, so the result needs qualification.
issues.quote: However, if lump sum taxing is not possible and all other taxes have a deadweight loss, we have $\lambda>u'$ and the Pigouvian tax -even at the optimal level- becomes attractive (MVPF\<1)

issues.text: The report notes the paper's cost-benefit ratio for a Pigouvian tax seems inconsistent: the pollution reduction lowers tax income equally, so the ratio is unaltered only when lambda equals u', and the presentation of this case is unclear.
issues.quote: As by the definition of a Pigouvian tax, the tax $\tau$ equals the externality V, the SVPF is unaltered. However for the cost-benefit ratio that is only the case for $\lambda=u'$.

issues.text: The report questions whether the constant elasticity of substitution assumption is appropriate, since it implies demand goes to infinity as price approaches zero, whereas realistic demand follows an S-shape, which the report argues leads to overestimated learning-by-doing gains.
issues.quote: Under constant elasticity, the demand goes to infinity as the price reaches zero. In reality demand follows an S-shape (for example a logistic shape).

issues.text: The report suggests the learning-by-doing estimates are relatively large because of a low 2% discount rate, the omission of exogenous time trends in costs, and the assumption that cost reductions are not due to reduced fixed costs.
issues.quote: I think the learning by doing estimates are relatively large for three other reasons, 1) a 2% discount rate is acceptable but relatively low, 2) the authors ignore exogenous time trend[s] in costs

issues.text: The report argues that the dynamic price effect is positive only when climate policy is suboptimal, and that the paper's treatment of the externality in the dynamic analysis is unclear; the evaluator suggests the net externality (SCC net of marginal abatement cost) may be the appropriate measure rather than the SCC.
issues.quote: It is a bit unclear how the externality V in equation 24 is defined. The authors only talk about the externality and I assume they use the SCC, where I would be inclined to use the SCC net of the MAC, as the net externality.

issues.text: The definition of the time variable t* in equation 23 is confusing, since it is not time zero (the time of the subsidy) while the lower bound of the integral in equation 22 uses time zero.
issues.quote: The definition of $t^\ast$ in equation 23 is confusing, because it is not really time zero (that is, the time of the subsidy, say 2025)

issues.text: The large size of transfers relative to environmental externalities, especially for subsidies, makes the marginal utility of winners and losers important; although the MVPF excludes this, the evaluator says it deserves more attention in the discussion.
issues.quote: That makes the question of the marginal utility of the winners and losers quite important. Although the MVPF is designed to exclude this effect, it is worth giving it more attention in the discussion.

issues.text: The report notes a notational inconsistency: the symbol lambda is used for the marginal utility of individuals in the paper but for the shadow price of the government budget constraint in the evaluator's equations.
issues.quote: (Secondary remark: in the paper, the $\lambda$ denotes the marginal utility of the individual, which is different from $ \lambda $ here.)
